findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt:119 NON_CV_CLOSE_DELAY_MS, consumed at line 1376 in scheduleNonCvClose and re-read in attemptNonCvClose at lines 1427-1443
findings.claim: The KDoc at lines 117-118 says the wait exists to give the popup time to render the Cruz Verde service node before deciding, and the first close attempt now fires at 200 ms instead of 500 ms, so a CV offer whose service node renders later than 200 ms is clicked closed as terminal CLOSED with no local record, since line 443 returns false and never registers the order. The untouched 300 ms verification and the two retries cannot rescue that case: they only confirm the popup disappeared or retry while it is still visible, so the residual exposure is a possibly lost CV order with recovery depending on the Picap app re-sending the offer. This is the documented exposure of the explicitly requested timing reduction, not a newly introduced defect.
proof_refs: MyAccessibilityService.kt line 119 sets NON_CV_CLOSE_DELAY_MS to 200L where it was 500L, and line 1376 delays the first attempt by that constant, so the first re-read and close decision now runs 200 ms after scheduling instead of 500 ms
KDoc lines 117 to 118 say the wait gives the popup time to render the Cruz Verde service node before deciding that it is not Cruz Verde

Lines 1427 to 1430 skip the close only when the servicio field is already non-empty at re-read time, otherwise line 1432 clicks the close button and lines 1437 to 1443 treat a vanished popup as terminal CLOSED with no retry
Line 443 returns false so the order is never added to the card or the history and non-CV closes are never memorized, leaving no local trace if a CV offer was dismissed too early
The 300 ms verification at line 1437 and its log strings at lines 1433 and 1439 are unchanged context in the diff, so the only behavioral change is the shortened pre-decision wait
